author: GitHub
description:
At Universe 2025, GitHub handed out Octolamps. Beatris Mendez Gandica wondered: what if hers could show when GitHub Copilot CLI is thinking? Using the native Copilot CLI hooks system, her lamp breathes green when the agent works, turns white when idle, and blinks red on errors via the WLED API. In this GitHub Universe 2026 session, Beatris shows how system-level lifecycle events connect software to physical hardware and how you can build custom hooks for any device. Explore the open-source repository to wire up your own WLED lights. 

Speakers: 
Bea Mendez Gandica, CEO/Founder, Nuevo Foundation

— CHAPTERS —  

00:00 Introduction and the octolamp idea
01:49 Understanding hooks in Copilot CLI
02:39 Configuring hooks and light states
04:17 Network architecture and fallbacks
05:02 Resolving hook race conditions
06:11 Live demo: Copilot CLI lamp indicator
08:55 Customization ideas and open-source repo
11:23 Audience Q&A and wrap up

#GitHubUniverse #GitHubCopilot #HardwareHacking

title: I made my Octolamp think with GitHub Copilot CLI hooks

author: GitHub
description:
Did you know the graphics on the GitHub Universe badge are actually capacitive touch buttons? In this clip from the GitHub Podcast, Martin Woodward breaks down how the conference badge transforms into a handheld gaming system. Learn how the official badge repository uses Copilot instructions so AI agents understand MicroPython and serial connections. With just a single prompt in the GitHub Copilot app, you can generate, test, and deploy a brand-new app directly to your badge hardware.
